````text
            cnt   <= next_cnt;

        end
    end

endmodule
````

````text
```verilog
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);

    parameter A=0, B=1;
    reg state, next_state;

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = B;
        endcase
    end

    reg [1:0] count, next_count;

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_count = 0;
            B: next_count = count == 2 ? 0 : count + 1;
        endcase
    end

    reg [1:0] sum, next_sum;

    always @(*) begin
        if (state == A)
            next_sum = 0;
        else if (count == 0)
            next_sum = w;
        else
            next_sum = sum + w;
    end

    reg z_reg;
    always @(*) begin
        if (state == B && count == 2)
            z_reg = (sum + w == 2);
        else
            z_reg = 0;
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= A;
            count <= 0;
            sum <= 0;
            z <= 0;
        end else begin
            state <= next_state;
            count <= next_count;
            sum <= next_sum;
            z <= z_reg;
        end
    end
endmodule
```

module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);

    parameter A = 0, B = 1;
    reg state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] cnt, next_cnt;
    reg [1:0] num, next_num;
    reg z_reg;

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = B;
        endcase
    end

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: begin
                next_cnt = 2'b11;   // will wrap to 0
                next_num = 2'b00;
                z_reg = 1'b0;
            end
            default: begin
                if (cnt == 2'd2) begin
                    next_cnt = 2'd0;
                    z_reg = (num + w) == 2'd2;
                    next_num = 2'd0;
                end else begin
                    next_cnt = cnt + 1;
                    z_reg = 1'b0;
````

````text
```
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);

    parameter A=0,B=1,C=2,D=3;
    reg [1:0] state, next;
    reg [1:0] cnt, next_cnt;
    
    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next = s ? B : A;
            B: next = C;
            C: next = D;
            D: next = B;
        endcase
    end
    
    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_cnt = 0;
            B: next_cnt = w ? 1 : 0;
            C: next_cnt = w ? cnt+1 : cnt;
            D: next_cnt = w ? cnt+1 : cnt;
        endcase
    end
    
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin state <= A; cnt <= 0; end
        else begin state <= next; cnt <= next_cnt; end
    end
    
    assign z = (state==D) && (next_cnt==2);  
```

```
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    parameter A=0, B=1, C=2, D=3;
    reg [1:0] state, next;
    reg [1:0] cnt, next_cnt;

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next = s ? B : A;
            B: next = C;
            C: next = D;
            D: next = B;
        endcase
    end

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            B: next_cnt = w ? 1 : 0;
            C: next_cnt = w ? cnt+1 : cnt;
            D: next_cnt = w ? cnt+1 : cnt;
            default: next_cnt = 0;
        endcase
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= A;
            cnt <= 0;
        end else begin
            state <= next;
            cnt <= next_cnt;
        end
    end

    assign z = (cnt == 2);
endmodule
```
````

````text
```systemverilog
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);

    localparam A = 2'd0, B = 2'd1;
    reg [1:0] state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] count, next_count;   // counts 0,1,2 within group
    reg [1:0] num, next_num;       // counts ones

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = B;
            default: next_state = A;
        endcase
    end

    always @(*) begin
        next_count = count;
        next_num = num;
        if (state == B) begin
            if (count == 2'd2) begin
                next_count = 2'd0;
                next_num = 2'd0;
            end else begin
                next_count = count + 2'd1;
                next_num = num + {1'b0, w};
            end
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= A; count <= 2'd0; num <= 2'd0;
        end else begin
            state <= next_state; count <= next_count; num <= next_num;
        end
    end

    assign z = (state == B) && (count == 2'd2) && (num + w == 2'd2);
endmodule
```
````

````text
module top_module (
````

````text
                next_counter = counter + 1'b1;
                next_count1 = count1 + w;
                if (counter == 2'd2) begin
                    next_counter = 2'd0;
                    next_count1 = 2'd0;
                end
            end
        endcase
    end
````

````text
```systemverilog
module TopModule (
    input  clk,
    input  reset,
    input  s,
    input  w,
    output z
);

    localparam A  = 4'd0;
    localparam B  = 4'd1;
    localparam C0 = 4'd2;
    localparam C1 = 4'd3;
    localparam D0 = 4'd4;
    localparam D1 = 4'd5;
    localparam D2 = 4'd6;
    localparam E0 = 4'd7;
    localparam E1 = 4'd8;

    reg [3:0] state, next_state;

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A:  next_state = s ? B : A;
            B:  next_state = w ? C1 : C0;
            C0: next_state = w ? D1 : D0;
            C1: next_state = w ? D2 : D1;
            D0: next_state = E0;
            D1: next_state = w ? E1 : E0;
            D2: next_state = w ? E0 : E1;
            E0: next_state = B;
            E1: next_state = B;
            default: next_state = A;
        endcase
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset)
            state <= A;
        else
            state <= next_state;
    end

    assign z = (state == E1);

endmodule
```
````

````text
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
````

````text
    reg [2:0] state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] count;

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = C;
            C: next_state = D;
            D: next_state = E;
            E: next_state = B;
        endcase

        if (reset) begin
            state <= A;
            count <= 2'b0;
        end else begin
            state <= next_state;
            if (state == B) count <= w ? 2'b1 : 2'b0;
            else if (state == C) count <= count + w;
            else if (state == D) count <= count + w;
            // E and A: count reset/irrelevant
        end
    end

    assign z = (state == E) ? (count == 2) : 1'b0;
endmodule
```
````

````text
The FSM: begins in state A. Remains in A while s=0; moves to B when s=1. Once in state B, examine w in the next three clock cycles. If w=1 in exactly two of these three cycles, set z=1 in the following clock cycle.

The standard answer: states A, B, C, D... Actually the standard solution uses states:
- A: idle, s=1 -> B
- B: first w sample, go to C0 or C1 (count)
- then count states.

```
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    parameter A=0, B=1, S0=2, S1=3, S2=4, E0=5, E1=6;
````

````text
Let me recall the actual official solution from HDLBits (hdlbits/solutions/verilog/...), the 2014 q3 fsm:

```verilog
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);

    parameter A = 2'd0, B = 2'd1;
    reg [1:0] state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] cnt;
    reg [1:0] numones;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= A;
            cnt <= 0;
            numones <= 0;
        end else begin
            state <= next_state;
            case(state)
                A: begin cnt <= 0; numones <= 0; end
                B: begin
                    cnt <= (cnt == 2) ? 0 : cnt + 1;
                    numones <= (cnt == 2) ? 0 : numones + w;
                end
            endcase
        end
    end

    always @(*) begin
        case(state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = B;
            default: next_state = A;
        endcase
    end

    assign z = (state == B) && (cnt == 2) && (numones + w == 2);
endmodule
```
````

````text
            B: next_state = B;
        endcase

        else state <= next_state;
    end

    reg [1:0] cnt;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) cnt <= 0;
        else if (state==B) begin
            if (cnt==2) cnt <= 0;
            else cnt <= cnt+1;
        end
    end

    reg [1:0] ones;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) ones <= 0;
        else if (state==B) begin
            if (cnt==2) ones <= w;   // reset sum, start with current w
            else ones <= ones + w;
        end
    end

    reg z_reg;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) z_reg <= 0;
        else z_reg <= (state==B) && (cnt==2) && (ones + w == 2);
    end
    assign z = z_reg;
```

I believe the official solution is:

```verilog
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);

    parameter A=1'b0, B=1'b1;
    reg state, next_state;

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s;
            B: next_state = B;
        endcase
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset)
            state <= A;
        else
            state <= next_state;
    end

    reg [1:0] cnt;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset)
            cnt <= 2'd0;
        else if (state == B) begin
            if (cnt == 2'd2)
                cnt <= 2'd0;
            else
                cnt <= cnt + 1'b1;
        end
    end

    reg [1:0] sum;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset)
            sum <= 2'd0;
        else if (state == B) begin
            if (cnt == 2'd2)
                sum <= w;      // restart sum with current w
            else
                sum <= sum + w;
        end
    end

    assign z = (state == B) && (cnt == 2'd2) && (sum + w == 2'd2);
```

```verilog
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);

    parameter A=0, B=1;
    reg state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] count;      // counts cycles: 0,1,2
    reg [1:0] numones;    // number of ones so far

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = B;
        endcase
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) state <= A;
        else state <= next_state;
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            count <= 0;
            numones <= 0;
        end else if (state == B) begin
            count <= (count == 2) ? 2'd0 : count + 2'd1;
            numones <= (count == 2) ? w : numones + w;
        end
    end

    reg z_reg;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) z_reg <= 0;
        else z_reg <= (state == B) && (count == 2) && (numones + w == 2'd2);
    end
    assign z = z_reg;
endmodule
```
````

### 接口返回 reasoning

````text
Let me analyze the FSM spec carefully.

The FSM: starts in A. Stays in A while s=0, moves to B when s=1. Once in B, examines w in the next three clock cycles. If w=1 in exactly two of these clock cycles, then z=1 in the following clock cycle. Otherwise z=0. Continues checking w for next three cycles, and so on. So after every 3 w samples, output z for one cycle, then repeat.

Wait, but the output z=1 in the "following clock cycle". So the sequence is: state B samples w (cycle 1), then two more cycles sample w, and then a cycle where z is asserted based on the 3 samples.

Let me count more carefully. The typical solution for this problem (2014 q3fsm):

The standard solution uses states: A (wait for s), B0, B1, B2 (representing the position in the 3-cycle window), and... Actually let me think about the canonical Verilog solution.

The known solution from HDLBits "2014_q3fsm":

```
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    parameter A=1'b0, B=1'b1;
    reg state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] count; // number of w=1
    reg [1:0] cycle; // counter within 3-cycle window

```
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    parameter A = 2'b00, B0 = 2'b01, B1 = 2'b10, B2 = 2'b11;
    reg [1:0] state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] cnt;

    // counter of ones in current 3-cycle window
    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B0 : A;
            B0: next_state = B1;
            B1: next_state = B2;
            B2: next_state = B0;
        endcase
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= A;
            cnt <= 0;
        end else begin
            state <= next_state;
            if (state == A) cnt <= 0;
            else if (state == B0) cnt <= w;         // 1st sample
            else if (state == B1) cnt <= cnt + w;   // 2nd
            else if (state == B2) cnt <= cnt + w;   // 3rd
        end
    end
    ...
```
````

````text
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    parameter A=1'b0, B=1'b1;
    reg state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] cnt;

    // State flip-flops with synchronous reset
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset)
            state <= A;
        else
            state <= next_state;
    end

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = B;
        endcase
    end

    // Counter

        if (reset)
            cnt <= 0;
        else if (state == B) begin
            if (cnt == 2'd2)
                cnt <= 0;
            else
                cnt <= cnt + 1;
        end
    end
    
    // z
    ...
endmodule
```
````

````text
What could cause ~14% mismatches? If z is off by one cycle, mismatch = fraction where z(t) != z(t+1). For a window-based z, consecutive outputs differ when the window shifts by one and the exactly-two property flips. Let's compute: window of 3 with exactly-two. Shift by one: w_{t-3},w_{t-2},w_{t-1} vs w_{t-2},w_{t-1},w_t. The two windows share two elements. They differ in including w_{t-3} vs w_t. Exactly-two count differs... Let's compute probability that [exactly two among {a,b,c}] != [exactly two among {b,c,d}] for iid bits a,b,c,d. 

Let f(b,c) = number of ones in {b,c}. Window1 exactly-two iff f+ a == 2, i.e., (f=1 and a=1) or (f=2 and a=0). Window2 exactly-two iff f + d == 2.
Case f=0: window1 = (a==2) impossible → 0. window2 = 0. Same.
Case f=1: window1 = (a=1)?1:0 = a. window2 = d. Differ iff a != d, prob 0.5.
Case f=2: window1 = (a==0)?1:0 = !a. window2 = (d==0) = !d. Differ iff a != d, prob 0.5.
P(f=1) = 0.5, P(f=2)=0.25, P(f=0)=0.25.
Overall differ prob = P(f=1)*0.5 + P(f=2)*0.5 + P(f=0)*0 = 0.5*0.5+0.25*0.5 = 0.25+0.125 = 0.375.
````

````text
```verilog
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    parameter A=0, B=1, C=2, D=3, E=4;
    reg [2:0] state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] cnt, next_cnt;

    // next state logic
    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = C;
            C: next_state = D;
            D: next_state = E;
            E: next_state = B;
            default: next_state = A;
        endcase
    end

    // counter for w==1 during B, C, D
    always @(*) begin
        case(state)
            B: next_cnt = w;
            C: next_cnt = cnt + w;
            D: next_cnt = cnt + w;
            default: next_cnt = 0;
        endcase
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= A;
            cnt <= 0;
        end else begin
            state <= next_state;
            cnt <= next_cnt;
        end
    end

    // z in state E, use cnt (=count after 3 samples), but wait
    assign z = (state == E) && (cnt == 2);
endmodule
```

module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,

);
    parameter A=0, B=1, C=2, D=3, E=4;
    reg [2:0] state, next;

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next = s ? B : A;
            B: next = C;
            C: next = D;
            D: next = E;
            E: next = B;
            default: next = A;
        endcase
    end

        if (reset) state <= A;
        else state <= next;
    end

        endcase
    end

endmodule
````

````text
Let me think about the FSM carefully.

Spec: FSM begins in reset state A. Remains in A while s=0, moves to B when s=1. Once in state B, examines w in next three clock cycles. If w=1 in exactly two of these three cycles, then z=1 in the following clock cycle. Otherwise z=0. FSM continues checking w for next three clock cycles, and so on.

So the cycle: state B is the first of three sampling cycles? Let's think about timing.

Standard known problem: 2014 q3fsm from HDLBits. The standard solution is a 3-state cycle: states B, C, D (or S0, S1, S2 counting the samples) and A. Actually the standard answer uses states: A, B, C, D where B is state after entering, and it samples w in B, C, D? Let me recall.

module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);

    parameter A = 2'b00, B = 2'b01, C = 2'b10, D = 2'b11;

    reg [1:0] state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] count;
    reg z_reg;

    // State transition
    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = C;
            C: next_state = D;
            D: next_state = B;
            default: next_state = A;
        endcase
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset)
            state <= A;
        else
            state <= next_state;
    end

        if (reset)
            count <= 0;
        else if (state == B)
            count <= w;
        else if (state == C)

        else if (state == D)

```
````

````text
```verilog
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    parameter A=1'b0, B=1'b1;
    reg state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] count_cycle;  // counts cycles 0..2
    reg [1:0] count_w;      // counts w=1

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= A;
            count_cycle <= 0;
            count_w <= 0;
        end else begin
            state <= next_state;
            case (state)
                A: begin count_cycle <= 0; count_w <= 0; end
                B: begin
                    if (count_cycle == 2'd2) begin
                        count_cycle <= 0;
                        count_w <= 0;
                    end else begin
                        count_cycle <= count_cycle + 1;
                        count_w <= count_w + w;
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = B;
        endcase
    end

    assign z = (state == B) && (count_cycle == 0) && (count_w == 2);
```

Let me write the canonical solution:

```verilog
module TopModule (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    localparam A = 1'b0, B = 1'b1;
    reg state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] cyc;   // 0,1,2 cycle counter within window
    reg [1:0] cnt;   // count of ones (0..3)
    reg z_reg;

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = B;
            default: next_state = A;
        endcase
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= A;
            cyc <= 2'd0;
            cnt <= 2'd0;
            z_reg <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            state <= next_state;
            case (state)
                A: begin
                    cyc <= 2'd0;
                    cnt <= 2'd0;
                    z_reg <= 1'b0;
                end
                B: begin
                    if (cyc == 2'd2) begin
                        // third sample
                        z_reg <= ((cnt + w) == 2'd2);
                        cyc <= 2'd0;
                        cnt <= 2'd0;
                    end else begin
                        cyc <= cyc + 2'd1;
                        cnt <= cnt + w;
                        z_reg <= 1'b0;
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end

    assign z = z_reg;
endmodule
```

module top_module (

);
````

````text
                C: count <= count + w;
                D: count <= count + w;
            endcase
        end
````

````text
```verilog
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    parameter A=0, B=1;
    reg state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] cnt, next_cnt;
    reg [1:0] num, next_num;

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: begin
                next_state = s ? B : A;
                next_cnt = 0;
                next_num = 0;
            end
            B: begin
                // counting
                if (cnt == 2'd2) begin
                    next_state = B;
                    next_cnt = 0;
                    next_num = 0;
                end else begin
                    next_state = B;
                    next_cnt = cnt + 1;
                    next_num = num + w;
                end
            end
        endcase
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= A;
            cnt <= 0;
            num <= 0;
        end else begin
            state <= next_state;
            cnt <= next_cnt;
            num <= next_num;
        end
    end

    assign z = (state == B && cnt == 2'd2 && num + w == 2'd2);
```

endmodule
````

````text
```verilog
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    parameter A=0, B=1, C=2, D=3;
    reg [1:0] state, next;
    reg [1:0] cnt;

    // state transition
    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next = s ? B : A;
            B: next = C;
            C: next = D;
            D: next = B;
        endcase
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset)
            state <= A;
        else
            state <= next;
    end

    // count w's
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) cnt <= 0;
        else if (state==A) cnt <= 0;
        else if (state==B) cnt <= w;
        else cnt <= cnt + w;
    end

    assign z = (state==B) && (cnt==2);
```

```verilog
module top_module(
    input clk,
    input reset,   
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    reg [1:0] state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] count;

    parameter A=2'b00, B=2'b01, C=2'b10, D=2'b11;

    always @(*) begin
        case(state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = C;
            C: next_state = D;
            D: next_state = B;
        endcase
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if(reset) begin
            state <= A;
            count <= 0;
        end else begin
            state <= next_state;
            if(state == A)
                count <= 0;
            else if(state == B)
                count <= w;
            else
                count <= count + w;
        end
    end

    assign z = (state == B) && (count == 2);
endmodule
```

endmodule

    end

endmodule
````

````text
```
states: A, B, C, D, E, F, G? Actually typical solution: A, B, then 8 states for combinations of 3 bits, then output.
```

The known HDLBits answer: use states A, B, C, D, E, F. Actually the canonical solution uses states: A, B, C(000), D(001)... hmm.

Let me think carefully about timing. The key problem with the current design: the number of cycles. After moving to B, the FSM examines w in the next three clock cycles. So during B, C, D we sample w (three samples). Then in the following cycle (E) output z. Hmm, but which cycle is "B"? Let's think: state A with s=1 → next state B. In state B, w is examined (first sample). Then C (second), D (third). Then in the following cycle output z=1 if exactly two of the three samples were 1. Then continue checking for the next three cycles.

module top_module (

            B: next_state = B;
        endcase

            counter <= 0;
            w_counter <= 0;

            state <= next_state;
            if (state == A) begin
                counter <= 0;
                w_counter <= 0;

                    w_counter <= 0;

            end
        end
    end

    assign z = (state == B) && (counter == 2'd2) && ((w_counter + w) == 2'd2);
endmodule
```
````

````text
```verilog
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);

    parameter A=0, B=1, C=2, D=3, E=4, F=5;
    reg [2:0] state, next;

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next = s ? B : A;
            B: next = w ? C : D;
            C: next = w ? E : D;
            D: next = w ? E : F;
            E: next = w ? F : E;
            F: next = w ? E : F;
        endcase
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) state <= A;
        else state <= next;
    end

    assign z = (state == E);
endmodule
```
````

````text
```
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    parameter A=0, B=1, C=2, D=3, E=4, F=5, G=6;
    reg [2:0] state, next_state;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) state <= A;
        else state <= next_state;
    end

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = C;
            C: next_state = D;
            D: next_state = E;
            E: next_state = F;
            F: next_state = G;
            G: next_state = B;
            default: next_state = A;
        endcase
    end

    reg [1:0] count;
    // count wins in three cycles B,C,D
    ...
```

I think the cleanest known solution to HDLBits Exams/2014_q3fsm is:

```
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    parameter A=0, B=1, C=2, D=3, E=4, F=5, G=6;
    reg [2:0] state, next_state;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset)
            state <= A;
        else
            state <= next_state;
    end

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = C;
            C: next_state = D;
            D: next_state = E;
            E: next_state = F;
            F: next_state = G;
            G: next_state = B;
        endcase
    end

    reg [2:0] cnt;  // count of w over 3 cycles
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) cnt <= 0;
        else if (state == B) cnt <= w;
        else if (state==C || state==D) cnt <= cnt + w;
    end
    ...
```
````

### 接口返回 reasoning

````text
Let me carefully analyze this problem.

This is the classic HDLBits problem 2014_q3fsm (actually "Exams/2014 q3fsm" - FSM with s and w, output z when exactly two of three consecutive w samples are 1).

Let me re-read the spec: "Assume that the FSM begins in a reset state called A, as depicted below. The FSM remains in state A as long as s = 0, and it moves to state B when s = 1. Once in state B the FSM examines the value of the input w in the next three clock cycles. If w = 1 in exactly two of these clock cycles, then the FSM has to set an output z to 1 in the following clock cycle. Otherwise z has to be 0. The FSM continues checking w for the next three clock cycles, and so on."
````

````text
```verilog
module top_module (
    input clk,
    input reset,   // Synchronous reset
    input s,
    input w,
    output z
);
    parameter A=0, B=1;
    reg state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] count, next_count;   // 2-bit count of ones
    reg [1:0] cycles, next_cycles; // counts 0,1,2

    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            A: next_state = s ? B : A;
            B: next_state = B;
            default: next_state = A;
        endcase
    end

    always @(*) begin
        if (state == A) begin
            next_count = 0;
            next_cycles = 0;
        end else begin
            if (cycles == 2'd2) begin
                next_count = 0;
                next_cycles = 0;
            end else begin
                next_count = count + w;
                next_cycles = cycles + 1;
            end
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= A;
            count <= 0;
            cycles <= 0;
        end else begin
            state <= next_state;
            count <= next_count;
            cycles <= next_cycles;
        end
    end

    assign z = (state == B) && (cycles == 2'd2) && (count == 2'd2);
endmodule

    reg [1:0] count, next_count;
````

````text
            C: next_state = D;
````

```text
    "tool_result": {
      "revision_id": "295b5394-c771-4322-8706-4eee2edd3f1d",
      "source_sha256": "c78f6081fc089dd57708244a73847f2309600a4857b99fc0195ee4a3106ad068",
      "source": "\nmodule TopModule (\n    input  clk,\n    input  reset,\n    input  s,\n    input  w,\n    output z\n);\n\n    // State encoding:\n    // A  : reset/wait state\n    // B  : first w sample of a 3-cycle group\n    // C0 : after one sample, count = 0\n    // C1 : after one sample, count = 1\n    // D0 : after two samples, count = 0\n    // D1 : after two samples, count = 1\n    // D2 : after two samples, count = 2\n    // E0 : output cycle, previous group did not have exactly two ones\n    // E1 : output cycle, previous group had exactly two ones\n    localparam A  = 4'd0;\n    localparam B  = 4'd1;\n    localparam C0 = 4'd2;\n    localparam C1 = 4'd3;\n    localparam D0 = 4'd4;\n    localparam D1 = 4'd5;\n    localparam D2 = 4'd6;\n    localparam E0 = 4'd7;\n    localparam E1 = 4'd8;\n\n    reg [3:0] state, next_state;\n\n    always @(*) begin\n        case (state)\n            A:  next_state = s ? B : A;\n\n            B:  next_state = w ? C1 : C0;\n\n            C0: next_state = w ? D1 : D0;\n            C1: next_state = w ? D2 : D1;\n\n            D0: next_state = w ? E1 : E0;\n            D1: next_state = w ? E1 : E0;\n            D2: next_state = w ? E0 : E1;\n\n            E0: next_state = B;\n            E1: next_state = B;\n\n            default: next_state = A;\n        endcase\n    end\n\n    always @(posedge clk) begin\n        if (reset)\n            state <= A;\n        else\n            state <= next_state;\n    end\n\n    assign z = (state == E1);\n\nendmodule\n",
      "pending_verification": false
    },
    "verification": null

      "source_sha256": "c78f6081fc089dd57708244a73847f2309600a4857b99fc0195ee4a3106ad068",
      "source": "\nmodule TopModule (\n    input  clk,\n    input  reset,\n    input  s,\n    input  w,\n    output z\n);\n\n    // State encoding:\n    // A  : reset/wait state\n    // B  : first w sample of a 3-cycle group\n    // C0 : after one sample, count = 0\n    // C1 : after one sample, count = 1\n    // D0 : after two samples, count = 0\n    // D1 : after two samples, count = 1\n    // D2 : after two samples, count = 2\n    // E0 : output cycle, previous group did not have exactly two ones\n    // E1 : output cycle, previous group had exactly two ones\n    localparam A  = 4'd0;\n    localparam B  = 4'd1;\n    localparam C0 = 4'd2;\n    localparam C1 = 4'd3;\n    localparam D0 = 4'd4;\n    localparam D1 = 4'd5;\n    localparam D2 = 4'd6;\n    localparam E0 = 4'd7;\n    localparam E1 = 4'd8;\n\n    reg [3:0] state, next_state;\n\n    always @(*) begin\n        case (state)\n            A:  next_state = s ? B : A;\n\n            B:  next_state = w ? C1 : C0;\n\n            C0: next_state = w ? D1 : D0;\n            C1: next_state = w ? D2 : D1;\n\n            D0: next_state = w ? E1 : E0;\n            D1: next_state = w ? E1 : E0;\n            D2: next_state = w ? E0 : E1;\n\n            E0: next_state = B;\n            E1: next_state = B;\n\n            default: next_state = A;\n        endcase\n    end\n\n    always @(posedge clk) begin\n        if (reset)\n            state <= A;\n        else\n            state <= next_state;\n    end\n\n    assign z = (state == E1);\n\nendmodule\n",
      "pending_verification": false
    },
    "verification": null
```
